1	/**
2	 * Consumer views, version 1: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
3	 *
4	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
5	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper
6	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"
7	 * what the source records.
8	 *
9	 * Contract (see `Transform`): the mapper receives every item one source published for one patient,
10	 * in no particular order and including items that were later superseded or retracted, plus an
11	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
12	 * date.
13	 *
14	 * Conventions for every view:
15	 *
16	 * - **Scope in time.** An item is in scope when its envelope `recorded` time is on or before the end of
17	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
18	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same
19	 *   issuer) is not current; supersession is transitive. Use only current items, except where a view
20	 *   below says otherwise.
21	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer displays everything in America/Chicago. "Local date" and "local time"
22	 *   below mean wall-clock date/time in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5 daylight time).
23	 * - **Partial dates.** `PartialDate` strings keep the precision the source actually knows: "2016"
24	 *   means some time in 2016, never 2016-01-01. Never pad a year-only or month-only date.
25	 * - **Only what the source records.** Rows come from structured payload entries. Narrative text may be
26	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.
27	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and payload entry ids) it was built from, so the consumer
28	 *   can show the source text behind a fact.
29	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output: no clock, randomness, network or file access.
30	 */

32	/** A FOLIO record item in its JSON form (see the FOLIO record-item spec). */
33	export interface FolioItem {
34	  folio: string;
35	  /** Item id (ULID), unique within the issuer. */
36	  id: string;
37	  /** did:web of the issuing organization. */
38	  issuer: string;
39	  /** Patient id at this issuer. */
40	  patient: string;
41	  /** When the clinical event happened: RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a full or partial date. */
42	  effective: string;
43	  effective_end?: string;
44	  /** When the issuer committed this item: RFC 3339 date-time with offset. */
45	  recorded: string;
46	  author?: { id?: string; name?: string; role?: string };
47	  /** The payload's schema: `type` names the entry type in the source's .d.ts. */
48	  schema?: { url: string; type: string; sha256: string };
49	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that this item replaces entirely. */
50	  supersedes?: string[];
51	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that were entered in error, withdrawn without replacement. */
52	  retracts?: string[];
53	  /** Markdown narrative with `<ref id="…">…</ref>` spans; "" if none. */
54	  narrative: string;
55	  /** Entry id -> entry, each entry typed by the source's schema; {} if none. */
56	  payload: Record<string, any>;
57	}

## ED provider note

**Chief complaint:** nausea, vomiting and shortness of breath.

**History.** The patient has type 2 diabetes and reports several days of vomiting and very little to eat or drink. Today she became weak and breathless and came in. Her home list includes <ref id="med_empagliflozin">empagliflozin 10 mg daily</ref>, not yet reconciled. Also on the list and not yet reconciled: metformin 500 mg twice daily, glipizide 5 mg daily, insulin glargine 10 units nightly and atorvastatin 40 mg nightly. No known drug allergies.

**Exam.** At 17:26: BP 114/68, HR 106, RR 18, T 99.1 F, SpO2 94%. She appears dry and uncomfortable, with deep breathing. Abdomen soft with mild diffuse tenderness.

**Results.** Venous gas: pH 7.16, pCO2 26. Beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.7. <ref id="bmp">Basic metabolic panel at 17:46: sodium 130, potassium 4.6, chloride 97, bicarbonate 13, anion gap 20, urea nitrogen 29, creatinine 2.15, eGFR 34, glucose 155.</ref>

**Assessment and plan**

1. <ref id="dx_dka">Diabetic ketoacidosis, euglycemic</ref>: pH 7.16, bicarbonate 13, anion gap 20 and beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.7 with a glucose of 155. Insulin infusion per DKA protocol at 0.1 units/kg/h started 18:30, with D5 lactated Ringer's at 150 mL/h. Admit to the hospitalist service.
2. <ref id="dx_pancreatitis">R/O pancreatitis</ref> given the abdominal tenderness and vomiting; lipase was drawn with the 17:46 labs and is pending at the time of this note.
3. Hyponatremia and elevated creatinine, consistent with volume depletion; fluids as above.

**Reason for admission:** euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis.

**Hospital course.** The patient presented with nausea, weakness and fast breathing and was found to have a severe anion gap acidosis with a glucose of only 242. **Condition at discharge.** Vitals at 09:00: BP 130/78, HR 89, RR 17, T 98.7 F, SpO2 96%. She feels well and is eating. The final basic metabolic panel at 06:28 showed sodium 135, potassium 4.0, chloride 99, bicarbonate 24, anion gap 12, urea nitrogen 18, creatinine 1.36 (eGFR 60) and glucose 165. Kidney function is much improved from admission.

**Allergies:** no known drug allergies.

**Medications at discharge**

- <ref id="med_dapagliflozin">Dapagliflozin 10 mg daily: do not resume until reviewed by her PCP</ref>
- <ref id="med_metformin">Metformin 1000 mg twice daily with meals: continue</ref>
- <ref id="med_lisinopril">Lisinopril 20 mg daily: continue</ref>
- <ref id="med_hydrochlorothiazide">Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily: continue</ref>

**Follow-up.** See her primary care physician at Northgate Family Medicine within 1 week to decide whether dapagliflozin should be restarted and to recheck a basic metabolic panel. She should return to the ED for vomiting, abdominal pain, fast breathing or marked weakness.

## Admission history and physical

**Reason for admission:** euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis.

**History of present illness.** The patient was seen in the ED this afternoon with malaise and a sense of being unwell, and was found to be markedly acidotic with a glucose of only 242. No clear precipitant was identified: no infection, no missed meals reported, no alcohol, no recent surgery. She takes dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for diabetes.

**Allergies:** no known drug allergies.

**Exam.** Vitals at 20:56: BP 110/66, HR 80, RR 21, T 98.2 F, SpO2 98%. Mildly tachypneic with deep respirations, appears somewhat dry.

**Results.** The basic metabolic panel drawn at 16:17 showed sodium 134, potassium 5.3, chloride 94, bicarbonate 8, anion gap 32, urea nitrogen 35, creatinine 1.57 (eGFR 50) and glucose 242. The insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/h and D5 lactated Ringer's at 150 mL/h have both been running since 17:05.

**Assessment and plan**

1. <ref id="dx_dka">Euglycemic DKA, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated</ref>. Continue the insulin infusion per DKA protocol with D5 lactated Ringer's, since glucose is not high. Repeat BMP every 4 hours until the gap closes. <ref id="med_dapagliflozin">Hold dapagliflozin.</ref>
2. Metformin: <ref id="med_metformin">hold metformin</ref> while she is acidotic and NPO.
3. Volume depletion with creatinine 1.57: <ref id="med_hydrochlorothiazide">hold hydrochlorothiazide</ref> until volume is restored.
4. Hypertension with potassium 5.3: <ref id="med_lisinopril">hold lisinopril</ref> for volume depletion and potassium; resume when she is eating and the potassium and creatinine have settled.
5. Hyperkalemia is mild and should improve with insulin and fluids; recheck with the next panel.

I wrote `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks with `sh in/harness/check.sh` and runs cleanly on both sample patients at several `asOf` dates. I also ran it on empty input, malformed items, and a made-up correction document that supersedes a discharge summary; it didn't throw, and it picked up the superseding copy and the corrected lab value. Nobody has checked the output against expected answers, since none were provided.

The judgment calls:

- **Which medication list counts:** I use the latest encounter's most recent discharge summary, as the schema says. If that stay has no discharge summary yet, I use the latest document that has a list. Drugs missing from that list are not reported. Statuses map as: not reconciled → `unknown`; continue, new and changed → `active`; held → `held`; stopped → `stopped`.
- **Held, advised against restarting:** dapagliflozin ("Do not resume until reviewed by PCP") stays `held`, not `stopped`. The schema says the outpatient prescriber makes the final call.
- **`status_since` for medications:** For held or stopped drugs, I walk back through earlier documents while the same drug and dose kept that status. The first such document's local date is used, so dapagliflozin is held since 2025-06-24 (the H&P), not the discharge date. For active drugs, I give a date only when the source shows a start: a `new` or `changed` line, or a resume after a hold (metformin resumed 2025-06-26). A plain `continue` gets no date, because the source never says when it started.
- **Drug-associated DKA:** "Euglycemic DKA, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated" (code RRH-DX-4471) produces two rows: a problem row for the DKA, and an `adverse_reaction` allergy row with high criticality. The diagnosis names a drug class, so I matched it to the one SGLT2 inhibitor on that stay's home list (dapagliflozin for one patient, empagliflozin for the other). This uses data within this source only. Diagnoses with ICD-10 T-codes for adverse drug effects become allergy rows only, not problems.
- **Problems:** "Working" diagnoses are left out unless a later document confirms them, and "ruled out" ones are left out entirely. The ED's uncoded "Diabetic ketoacidosis, euglycemic" (E11.10) is merged with the later RRH-DX-4471 entries, because the hospital code is more precise than the shared ICD-10 code. I don't report an onset for diagnoses. Onsets come only from history lines with a clear year, month or full date. For CKD stage, I prefer clinicians' diagnoses over history lines, which the schema warns can be out of date.
- **Allergies:** I use the latest document's list, and "NKDA" produces no row. The reaction text decides allergy vs. intolerance vs. adverse reaction. Mild maps to low criticality and severe to high; I mapped moderate to `unknown`.
- **Labs:** One row per accession plus test code, taken from the copy with the most advanced status (corrected, then final, then preliminary). If that copy's value isn't a number (e.g. "Hemolyzed"), the result is dropped rather than falling back to an older copy. I convert units only when I recognise them; otherwise the result is skipped. eGFR variants with a race coefficient are dropped. The eGFR equation is read from the test name first, then the LOINC code, then the schema's rule that results since 2023 are CKD-EPI 2021.
- **Vitals:** Sets with no blood pressure, pulse or weight are skipped. A second blood pressure within 30 minutes in the same stay is recorded as a repeat on the earlier row; the samples don't contain this case, so it's untested.

My two scratch scripts, `out/show.ts` and `out/robust.ts`, are still in `out/`; only `transform.ts` is used.
